title: PathFuzz: Broadening Fuzzing Horizons with Footprint Memory for CPUs
problem: Coverage-guided fuzzing for CPU verification is hindered by limited seed corpus sources and inefficient mutation strategies, preventing effective test input generation for achieving high verification coverage.
motivation: Improving CPU verification coverage through better fuzzing methods enables identification of subtle bugs in real-world CPU designs that traditional verification approaches miss.
method: PathFuzz takes two complementary approaches to generate test inputs that expose CPU design flaws. First, it uses footprint memory—a compact input format tailored to CPU architecture—combined with real-world software examples as seed inputs. Second, it applies coverage-guided fuzzing (a technique that mutates test inputs while tracking which CPU behaviors each input exercises) with improved mutation strategies to automatically discover high-impact test cases.
key_novelty: Footprint memory is a compact, CPU-specific input format that replaces inefficient generic test-generation methods used in standard fuzzing.
contributions: Proposes footprint memory as an efficient input format for CPU fuzzing
Incorporates seed corpus from real-world programs to improve coverage guidance
Achieves 95%+ verification coverage on CPU designs
Identifies four long-standing bugs in well-known open-source CPU implementations
